taxonomyNote: Now Urocitellus; ADW uses the older Spermophilus. NatureServe: ground squirrels formerly in Spermophilus are split into 8 genera (Helgen et al. 2009).
fieldMarks: Stout body with short dense fur
Dorsum light pinkish or cinnamon buff with a dappled rear; countershaded lighter belly
Darker cinnamon buff on front of forelegs, neck and sides of head; light buff eye ring
Tail black above, cinnamon or clay below, edged pinkish buff
behavior: Hibernates, entering late August-October and emerging by late March or April
Activity peaks about 2 h after dawn, 10 am-2 pm and 4 pm to sunset; stays in the burrow in extreme heat or rain
Multi-syllable alarm calls vary with predator type
Eats herbaceous plants in spring, seeds and fruit in late summer and fall; stores seeds in burrows; loose colonies
habitat: Grasslands, rolling hills, fields and croplands; prefers gravelly or sandy soil and short grass around burrow entrances.
range: Northern Great Plains: southern Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba, Montana, North Dakota, northeastern South Dakota, western Minnesota and northwestern Iowa.
